selected_mechanism.name: FERC preliminary permit site-banking under FPA sec. 4(f) / 16 U.S.C. 798, and the 18 CFR 4.32(e) deficiency-and-acceptance gate that manufactures the priority date
selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: A FERC preliminary permit authorizes no construction whatsoever. Its only legal effect is to freeze a first-in-time priority to file a hydropower license application over a defined water corridor for up to four years, extendable four more. Whether an applicant keeps its original filing date, and therefore its priority, is decided by a paperwork-conformance determination inside FERC's Office of Energy Projects, and no competing party can file against the corridor until that determination goes the applicant's way.

news_trigger.verbatim_quote: An East Coast company has proposed building an underwater artificial intelligence data center, powered by the strong tides of Cook Inlet, off the shore of Nikiski. Delaware-based DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC released plans for a 100-megawatt data center project with as many 350 underwater turbines and 66 "hives" housing AI servers, both powered and cooled by water of Cook Inlet.
news_trigger.why_underexplained: ADN reported the proposal, the June 18 deficiency letter from the Northwest Branch Division of Hydropower Licensing, and that FERC 'found a number of deficiencies.' It never explains what the instrument is. The article never once uses the phrase 'preliminary permit', it says only that Wolfson 'sent in an application to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to conduct preliminary environmental and engineering studies.' A reader therefore cannot learn that the filing confers priority-in-time over a 1,650-acre corridor and no construction right; that the cure window is capped at 45 days and a rejection resets the filing date to the back of the queue; that no Alaska party can file a competing application until FERC accepts the application; or that an uncontested preliminary permit is acted on by one delegated office rather than by the five commissioners.

layers.layer: Layer 1, the corridor claim, what an applicant must put on paper to bank a stretch of water
layers.what_it_does: Fixes the contents of a preliminary permit application. Exhibit 1 project description, Exhibit 2 study plan, Exhibit 3 maps that must enclose a proposed project boundary. This is where a 1,650-acre operational envelope either is or is not adequately described, and it is the layer FERC's June 18 deficiency letter attacked.
layers.controlling_actor: The applicant, DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, Louis Wolfson managing member (Needham, Massachusetts); DeepGreen Holdings LLC formed January 2026, one month before filing
layers.primary_source_type: CFR (18 CFR 4.81, contents of preliminary permit application)
layers.evidence_quote: All lands of the United States that are enclosed within the proposed project boundary.

layers.layer: Layer 2, the deficiency-and-acceptance gate, where the priority date is kept or destroyed
layers.what_it_does: One office judges whether the application conforms. If it does not, the applicant gets a cure window capped at 45 days for a preliminary permit. If the revised application still does not conform, or the cure is late, it is rejected, and any resubmission carries a NEW filing date, collapsing the site-priority claim to the back of the queue. Conformance instead produces acceptance for filing, a project number, and a fixed acceptance date.
layers.controlling_actor: Director, FERC Office of Energy Projects (the regulation vests the judgment in this office; the 18 June 2026 letter to DeepGreen issued from the Northwest Branch, Division of Hydropower Licensing, under that authority)
layers.evidence_quote: An application that in the judgment of the Director of the Office of Energy Projects does not conform to the requirements of paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) of this section and of § 4.38, may be considered deficient. ... An applicant having a deficient application will be afforded additional time to correct deficiencies, not to exceed 45 days from the date of notification in the case of an application for a preliminary permit or exemption from licensing ... The date the rejected application is resubmitted will be considered the new filing date for purposes of determining its timeliness under § 4.36 and the disposition of competing applications under § 4.37.

layers.layer: Layer 3, what the instrument actually buys, statutory priority and nothing else
layers.what_it_does: Defines the asset being contested. Congress authorized preliminary permits for the sole purpose of maintaining priority of application for a license, for a term not exceeding four years, extendable once by up to four more on a showing of good faith and reasonable diligence, and non-transferable. No construction right, no entry right, no property interest.
layers.controlling_actor: Congress, via FPA section 4(f) as codified; the Commission exercising the term discretion Congress granted
layers.evidence_quote: Each preliminary permit issued under this subchapter shall be for the sole purpose of maintaining priority of application for a license ... Such permits shall not be transferable, and may be canceled by order of the Commission upon failure of permittees to comply with the conditions thereof or for other good cause shown after notice and opportunity for hearing.

layers.layer: Layer 4, public notice, and the moment Alaska parties first acquire standing
layers.what_it_does: Only once FERC accepts the application does the Secretary issue a notice opening the window in which anyone else, a utility, a borough, a tribe, a state authority, may intervene or file a competing preliminary permit application over the same waters. 18 CFR 4.36 ties competing filings to the intervention deadline prescribed in that notice; FERC's standard practice in Cook Inlet preliminary permit notices has been 60 days from issuance. Until the notice issues, no Alaska party can obtain competing priority.
layers.controlling_actor: Kimberly D. Bose, Secretary, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (issues the notice); 18 CFR 4.36 governs the competing filings
layers.primary_source_type: FERC notice, Federal Register public-inspection PDF (Project No. 15317-000, Littoral Power Systems, Upper Cook Inlet Tidal Energy Project, dated 5 Sept 2023)
layers.evidence_quote: The sole purpose of a preliminary permit is to grant the permit holder priority to file a license application during the permit term. A preliminary permit does not authorize the permit holder to perform any land-disturbing activities or otherwise enter upon lands or waters owned by others without the owners' express permission. ... Comments, motions to intervene, competing applications (without notices of intent), or notices of intent to file competing applications should be submitted within 60 days from the issuance of this notice. Competing applications and notices of intent must meet the requirements of 18 CFR 4.36.

layers.layer: Layer 5, the contested/uncontested fork, staff signature or five-member proceeding
layers.what_it_does: An uncontested preliminary permit application is acted on by the Director of the Office of Energy Projects under delegated authority, with no commissioner vote. A protest or opposed intervention flips the matter to the Commission itself. Whether any Alaska party files inside the prescribed deadline is therefore what decides whether this corridor is transferred by one delegated signature or litigated before five commissioners.
layers.controlling_actor: Director, FERC Office of Energy Projects (delegated authority)
layers.primary_source_type: CFR (18 CFR 375.308(a)(3), delegations to the Director, Office of Energy Projects)

chokepoint.actor: Director, FERC Office of Energy Projects (institutional role; branch staff act under this authority)
chokepoint.binary_decision: Determine that DeepGreen's cured application conforms, accepting it for filing, preserving its original filing date as the site-priority date, and triggering the Secretary's notice, or determine it does not conform, in which case any resubmission carries a new filing date and the priority claim over the Nikiski corridor collapses to the back of the queue.
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: A preliminary permit's entire value is priority in time; the statute says so in terms. That asset is manufactured by a paperwork-conformance call vested by regulation in a single office, made before any commissioner votes, before any environmental review, and before any Alaska party is legally able to file a competing application, because the competing-application window does not open until this office says the application is complete. The same office holds the delegated final action at Layer 5 on any uncontested permit. It is not a committee and not a hearing. It is a letter. FERC spokesperson Celeste Miller told ADN the application is still under review, so the determination is live as of the run date.

selected_mechanism.ak_consequence: Alaska electric utilities and grid infrastructure. The Alaska Energy Authority (CEO Curtis Thayer, who told ADN AEA had never heard of DeepGreen nor received any contact from the company), Homer Electric Association (whose Bernice Lake substation is the confirmed landfall for this corridor), the Kenai Peninsula Borough, and Kenai-area tribes and ANCSA corporations cannot intervene or file a competing application over the roughly 1,650-acre Nikiski corridor until FERC's Office of Energy Projects accepts DeepGreen's application, a determination pending now, after which the prescribed intervention clock (60 days in FERC's standard Cook Inlet preliminary-permit notices) starts running from issuance, not from discovery.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: This is site-banking, not power development. A Delaware SPV formed in January 2026, one month before it filed, is using a 1920 hydropower statute to place a four-to-eight-year exclusive priority claim over a stretch of Alaska seabed, using an instrument that costs almost nothing, confers no construction right, requires no environmental review to obtain, and is decided on paperwork conformance by one delegated office. The AI framing is not decoration. The compute load is what makes a tidal corridor in Cook Inlet worth optioning, because a 100 MW behind-the-meter buyer solves the offtake problem that has killed every prior Cook Inlet tidal proposal. The structural lesson for Alaska is about standing and timing, not about tidal power. The parties with the most to lose from a corridor claim, the state's own grid authority, the co-op at the landfall, the borough, the tribes, are structurally last to know and legally last to act, because the window that lets them object does not exist until the applicant has already cleared the only gate that matters. FERC has noticed a preliminary permit in this same corridor before, to Littoral Power Systems at P-15317-000, describing the identical geography and the same Homer Electric substation. The machinery recurs; the Alaska parties keep arriving after the clock starts.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: This week. AEA, Homer Electric Association and the Kenai Peninsula Borough should have a motion to intervene and, if warranted, a competing preliminary permit application drafted and ready to file BEFORE FERC issues the acceptance notice, not after. The deadline runs from notice issuance, and FERC does not extend it for parties who were not monitoring. Set an eLibrary docket alert on Cook Inlet hydrokinetic filings now. For allocators and developers, this is the cheap option-on-a-corridor play, and it is available to anyone with a competent Exhibit 3, which means Alaska-based parties can use it defensively on corridors their own projects need, at a fraction of the cost of contesting someone else's claim later.
selected_mechanism.recurrence: Fires at every preliminary permit application, in the same water. FERC previously noticed a preliminary permit for the Upper Cook Inlet Tidal Energy Project, Project No. 15317-000, sited approximately 17 miles north-northwest of Kenai and 9.5 miles northwest of Nikiski, the same corridor, with the same Homer Electric Bernice Lake substation as landfall. It fires again at each 45-day cure cycle, at each acceptance notice, at each intervention deadline, and at every four-year permit term and extension.
uncertainty_flags: The ADN article never uses the phrase 'preliminary permit.' It says Wolfson 'sent in an application to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to conduct preliminary environmental and engineering studies.' The identification of the instrument as an FPA sec. 4(f) preliminary permit is the desk's reading of that description against 16 U.S.C. 798 ('for making examinations and surveys') and against FERC's Northwest Branch Division of Hydropower Licensing handling it. This reading is sound but the writer must present it as the desk explaining what the filing IS, not as a phrase ADN used.

The 60-day figure is FERC's standard NOTICE practice, verified verbatim in the P-15317-000 notice. It is NOT a flat requirement of 18 CFR 4.36, which instead ties competing filings to the intervention deadline prescribed in the public notice. Do not write '18 CFR 4.36 gives 60 days.' Write that FERC's notice prescribes the deadline and has set 60 days in this corridor before.

The Cook Inlet PowerLink details (400 million dollars, 38-mile submarine line between Nikiski and Beluga) are as REPORTED BY ADN, and the tie-in claim is DeepGreen's own assertion. AEA's own website does not use the name 'Cook Inlet PowerLink'; it references a 'Railbelt Innovation Resiliency project' with a 206.5 million dollar grant for an HVDC submarine cable. Attribute to ADN; do not state as AEA-confirmed, and do not conflate the two project names.

_validation_note: TARGET SELECTED at 14 days; no broadening required. THE DISTINCTNESS CALL: the DeepGreen preliminary permit was judged sufficiently distinct from the 2026-08-14 Bradley Lake anatomy. Both are FERC hydropower and both touch the 18 CFR 375.308 delegated-authority layer, which is a real cost, not hidden. But the instrument, the subpart, the chokepoint and the consequence structure are all different: Bradley Lake was a non-capacity AMENDMENT to an existing 40-year license held by a state authority, decided on the merits via a delegated order. This is the PRE-LICENSE site-banking instrument under 16 U.S.C. 798, where the chokepoint is a paperwork-conformance determination under 4.32(e) that controls a FILING DATE, and where the Alaska story is about standing and timing rather than about what gets built. Nothing about the layer chain is re-mapped. The shared delegation layer is flagged so the writer draws the contrast explicitly. Decisive against the main rival: RGP-05 has the better document trail of any candidate this cycle, but the 32-page instrument never mentions compute, no AI applicant has filed, and its quantified Alaska consequence rested on advocacy-sourced acreage that could not be replaced. Taking it would have meant running an AI column about a gravel-fill permit on an inferred AI connection, which is precisely the confabulation this gate exists to stop. DeepGreen is the only candidate whose AI tie is documentary rather than analogical: the application is itself for an AI data center. THRESHOLD CONFLICT RESOLVED against primary text: FAR 19.808-1 states 30 million dollars with no DoD/civilian distinction; DFARS 219.808-1 returns 404; the Koniag marketing page's 25M/100M claim is wrong and the layer built on it was dropped. SCOUT ERRORS CORRECTED: (1) the ADN trigger quote was misquoted twice by the regulatory scout ('Cook Inlet's strong tides' should be 'the strong tides of Cook Inlet'; 'as many as 350' should be 'as many 350'), the corrected text above is what resolves on the live page; (2) the scout's '60-day competing-application window under 18 CFR 4.36' is a misreading, 4.36 prescribes a deadline set BY THE NOTICE, and the 60 days is FERC's notice practice, verified verbatim in the P-15317-000 notice; (3) the chokepoint actor is better and more verifiably identified as the Director, Office of Energy Projects, whom 4.32(e) names directly, which both eliminates the unverifiable branch-chief-name problem and strengthens the mechanism-not-actor gate. LAYER DROPPED: the Cook Inlet beluga critical habitat layer (50 CFR 226.220), containment within Area 2 could not be verified and was the scout's own inference. The chain stands at five layers without it. UNVERIFIABLE AND EXCLUDED: the FERC docket number (eLibrary unfetchable on four attempts), the deficiency-letter signatory, and whether an acceptance notice has issued. All are in do_not_assert; none is load-bearing. Category balance is the one editorial cost: this makes regulatory 4 of the last 7 issues, flagged rather than treated as a gate failure.
